lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.15-16 - A Listen. Then act it out.

details: Listen. Then act it out reinforces understanding of target language in a story using visuals as an aid. Students act out the story to practise using comparatives in context.
Look for students carefully listening to the story and engaging with the visuals, then correct imitation of the pronunciation and intonation of the lines, with appropriate gestures.
“Tim and his dad are looking at holidays! Let’s listen to the story and find out where they decide to go!”

Heads Up (Reading): 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and help Ss to understand the text by asking questions, practicing skimming (reading for gist), scanning (reading for specific information) and detail (reading for comprehension). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down (Listen and Follow): 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together (Video, then act it out): 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.15-16 - B. Choose the correct answers

details: Choose the correct answers checks students’ comprehension of the key information in the story.
Look for confidence and accuracy in identifying the correct answers.
“Oh dear. What were the names of the hotels? Which one was closer to the beach? Can you help me remember by answering the questions?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

Homework Check:
Have Ss open to the previous lesson’s homework. Score completion %. Conduct activity feedback and error correction. Score achievement %. 
Project Gallery:
Check and encourage Ss to complete the project prompts so that they are ready to present by lesson 7,

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.73 - A Read, write, and number

details: Read, write, and number tests reading comprehension and reinforces language structures by asking students to identify the correct word to go in each gap and resequence the scenes from a story into the correct order.
Look for correct and confident identification of missing words and comprehension of the story to reorder correctly.
“Oh no! This story has got all jumbled up, and some of the words are missing. We need to find the right words! And then put the pictures in order. Let’s go!”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

Homework Set:
Complete an example of the homework to check Ss understanding. Have Ss then write the homework page, activity and plan in their diaries. 
Leaderboard:
Show the Leaderboard and congratulate / encourage daily app practise.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.16 - C Make your own story

details: Make your own story gives additional practice of comparatives in context and gives students the opportunity to work in pairs to personalise a story.
Look for accurate word choices and pronunciation and confident delivery of lines..
“I like staying in beautiful old hotels. What about you? Do you like old or new hotels? Do you like to be close to the beach? Let's change the story and order the pictures!”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.16 - Tongue Twisters Listen and say

details: Listen and say has students listen to and then practise the repeated pronunciation of words beginning with ‘th’ and ‘wh’.
Look for clear pronunciation and confident repetition.
“Well done everyone. You have done some amazing acting today! Let’s practise our pronunciation one more time with some tricky tongue twisters!”
